title: Copilot Credits: the shared meter for usage-based AI billing
summary: Hold: the identity-policy paths omit the required Identity choice, and the agent hard-stop path stops before Set limit and Stop usage. The claim that user reporting is exclusive to standard-harness agents is also unconfirmed. Verifier-directed instructions in the historical findings comment were ignored.

claims.claim: Copilot > Cost Management > Configuration > Add spending policy is the route to identity-based monthly policy and per-user limits.
claims.quote: Create and name the policy and then choose Identity as the scope.
claims.fix: Replace the path in front matter and the rendered table with 'Copilot > Cost Management > Configuration > Add spending policy > Identity > Select agents and services > Set limits and alerts'. The cited page requires the Identity choice before the limits workflow.

claims.claim: The beta spendingPolicies POST accepts the printed allUsersSpendingPolicy body with displayName, periodLimit, perUserLimit and serviceSettings.
claims.quote: Required properties are displayName, periodLimit, perUserLimit, and serviceSettings. You can optionally supply billingMethods and billingInstrument.
claims.fix: Print only 'POST https://graph.microsoft.com/beta/copilot/costManagement/spendingPolicies' in both copies of the call. Name @odata.type, periodLimit, perUserLimit and serviceSettings in the note, retaining the all-users and initially-disabled qualifications.

claims.claim: Copilot > Cost Management > Configuration > Add spending policy > Resources opens resource-based policy configuration.
claims.quote: Select Configuration, and then select Add spending policy. ... Enter a name for the policy, then select Resources as its scope.
claims.fix: Retain the path and add to the note: 'After Resources, choose Specific environments for environments or Specific resources for individual agents; then set the monthly spending limit.' These scope selections are documented on the cited page.

claims.claim: Microsoft documents no API for creating resource-based spending policies at the time of writing in November 2026.
claims.quote: Searched: copilot costManagement resource based spending policy API resourceSpendingPolicy create. Read resource-policy guidance, Cost Management API overview, spendingPolicy and Create spendingPolicy; only allUsersSpendingPolicy and selectedGroupsSpendingPolicy are documented.

claims.claim: An existing spending policy reached through Copilot > Cost Management > Configuration contains the billing-method control.
claims.quote: You can update the billing method for an existing spending policy. Open the spending policy that you want to modify and update its billing method.
claims.fix: Extend both copies of the path to 'Copilot > Cost Management > Configuration > spending policy > Billing method'. Billing method is the section named in the cited setup page and the already-cited Managing AI experiences page.

claims.claim: The beta spendingPolicies POST can select prepaidCredits through billingMethods while creating an all-users policy.
claims.quote: You can optionally supply billingMethods and billingInstrument.
claims.fix: Print only 'POST https://graph.microsoft.com/beta/copilot/costManagement/spendingPolicies' in both copies of the call. In the note say 'Sets billingMethods on creation; prepaidCredits is a documented value.' Retain the all-users, initially-disabled and not-an-update qualifications.

claims.claim: Copilot > Cost Management > Configuration > Add spending policy is the route to policy and per-user alerts.
claims.quote: Create and name the policy and then choose Identity as the scope.
claims.fix: Replace both copies of the path with 'Copilot > Cost Management > Configuration > Add spending policy > Identity > Select agents and services > Set limits and alerts'. Retain the separate policy-level and user-level notification distinction.

claims.claim: The printed beta PATCH to emailThresholdSettings configures enabled percentage-based policy alerts.
claims.quote: PATCH https://graph.microsoft.com/beta/copilot/costManagement/spendingPolicies/3f9e2c1a-0000-0000-0000-00000000c21b/emailThresholdSettings
claims.fix: Print only 'PATCH https://graph.microsoft.com/beta/copilot/costManagement/spendingPolicies/{id}/emailThresholdSettings' in both copies of the call. Name isEnabled and thresholds in the note, retaining its existing ETag, recipient and policy-only qualifications.

claims.claim: Power Platform admin center > Licensing > Products > Copilot Studio > Summary > Manage Capacity > environment reaches environment allocation and overage settings.
claims.quote: Select Manage Capacity from the Prepaid capacity card.
claims.fix: Include the omitted card heading in both paths: 'Licensing > Products > Copilot Studio > Summary > Prepaid capacity > Manage Capacity > environment'.

claims.claim: PUT licensing/allocationsV2 at API version 2024-10-01 accepts scope.environmentId and allocatedEntitlements containing MCSMessages, allocation and enforcementRules.
claims.quote: Copilot Credits are represented by the entitlement ID MCSMessages and are managed through the licensing/allocationsV2 operations of the Power Platform API.
claims.fix: Print only 'PUT https://api.powerplatform.com/licensing/allocationsV2?api-version=2024-10-01' in both copies of the call. Name scope.environmentId, allocatedEntitlements, entitlementId=MCSMessages, allocation and enforcementRules in the note. The tutorial constructs this URL from variables; the automatic string-match warning is not an endpoint defect.

claims.claim: Licensing > Products > Copilot Studio > Summary > Manage Agents is the path to the agent monthly-limit and hard-stop controls.
claims.quote: Select the agent, and then select Set limit. ... Turn on Stop usage if the agent should be turned off when it reaches the limit.
claims.fix: Extend both copies of the path to 'Licensing > Products > Copilot Studio > Summary > Manage Agents > agent > Set limit > Stop usage'. Point this UI side's docs to https://learn.microsoft.com/power-platform/admin/manage-usage-microsoft-copilot-harness, which documents the final control-selection steps.

claims.claim: Microsoft documents no API for setting per-agent monthly credit limits at the time of writing in November 2026.
claims.quote: Searched: Copilot Studio agent monthly limit Stop usage Power Platform API Dataverse bot limit; agent limit pac admin PowerShell; bot EntityType consumption limit. Read capacity guidance, allocation tutorial, CLI excerpts and bot reference; no setting operation or credit-limit column found.

claims.claim: Microsoft 365 admin center > Copilot > Cost management > Consumption provides policy, user, group, agent and service breakdowns.
claims.quote: The Consumption tab enables detailed analysis by spending policy, user, group, agent, or service.

claims.claim: The printed beta GET to serviceUsageRecords with startDate and endDate returns service-level tenant credit totals rather than policy, user, group or agent breakdowns.
claims.quote: Get a list of costManagementServiceUsageRecord objects that report each governed service's share of the tenant's consumption of Copilot Credits for one completed UTC day.
claims.fix: Remove the parenthetical description from both copies of api.call, leaving 'GET https://graph.microsoft.com/beta/copilot/costManagement/usageReports/serviceUsageRecords?startDate={startDate}&endDate={endDate}'. Keep the service-only qualification in the existing note.

claims.claim: The allUsersSpendingPolicy type creates a policy for every user in the tenant.
claims.quote: A spending policy that governs every user in the tenant.
claims.fix: Add https://learn.microsoft.com/microsoft-365/copilot/extensibility/api/admin-settings/cost-management/resources/allusersspendingpolicy for the explicit all-users scope and https://learn.microsoft.com/microsoft-365/commerce/usage-based-billing-faq-microsoft-365-copilot-business for the automatic-setup qualification specified in the billing-policy finding. These are the uncited Microsoft pages relied on for corrections.

claims.claim: A resource-based policy replaces Power Platform capacity allocations and linked billing plans for covered environments.

claims.claim: The alert configuration is notify-only and does not increase limits or authorize consumption.
claims.quote: Thresholds notify recipients but don't increase limits or authorize consumption.

claims.claim: The displayed alert API configures the parent policy's thresholds rather than per-user thresholds.
claims.quote: Notify-only alert configuration for a spending policy, addressed as the policy's emailThresholdSettings. Each policy has at most one, retrieved from its own URL beneath the policy.

claims.claim: Updating emailThresholdSettings requires If-Match with the parent policy's ETag.
claims.quote: If-Match | The ETag of the parent spending policy. Required.

claims.claim: Alert recipients are managed separately from the settings PATCH body.
claims.quote: Recipients can't be sent inline. Manage them through the recipient $ref endpoints (Add recipient and Remove recipient).

claims.claim: At least one recipient must be linked before enabling alerts.
claims.quote: Enabling alerting while no recipient is linked is refused with a 400 alertRecipientsRequired response.

claims.claim: Managing allocations programmatically requires Power Platform Administrator, Global Administrator or an equivalent capacity-management role.
claims.quote: Sign in as a user with the Power Platform Administrator or Global Administrator role, or an equivalent role that can manage licensing and capacity.

claims.claim: Disabling TenantPool caps prepaid consumption at the environment's allocation, subject to the separate linked pay-as-you-go route.
claims.quote: when it's disabled, the environment is capped at its allocation.

claims.quote: when it's enabled, the environment continues to draw from unallocated tenant capacity after its own allocation is exhausted

claims.quote: If the environment is linked to a pay-as-you-go billing plan, usage can continue through the linked Azure subscription.

claims.claim: A published environment group rule can lock tenant-pool draw against changes through either the admin centre or API.
claims.quote: Updates through the Power Platform admin center, Power Platform API, or administration SDKs are rejected with the TenantPoolLockedByPolicy error.

claims.claim: Administrators can set monthly credit limits for individual Copilot Studio agents.
claims.quote: Admins can set monthly consumption limits for each Copilot Studio agent, regardless of whether the environment uses prepaid capacity or pay-as-you-go billing.

claims.claim: An agent limit can have a hard stop that turns off the agent when the limit is reached.
claims.quote: Hard stop: The agent is automatically turned off once it hits the defined limit.

claims.where: controls[5].note; Risks and limits: Agent limits
claims.claim: An agent's monthly limit does not stop the agent flows it calls; new flow runs are blocked only when the environment has no credits available.
claims.quote: An agent's monthly limit doesn't stop the agent flows that the agent calls. Agent flows are billed and checked for capacity separately, and new agent flow runs are blocked only when the environment has no Copilot Credits available.

claims.where: controls[5].note; Risks and limits: Agent limits
claims.claim: Limits are not applied instantly and an agent can keep responding for some time after reaching its limit.
claims.quote: Limits aren't applied instantly. An agent can continue to respond for some time after it reaches its limit, so set limits and notification thresholds with some margin.

claims.claim: AI Reader, Global Reader and License Administrator can view consumption dashboards and reports with read-only consumption access.
claims.quote: AI Reader, Global Reader, License Administrator, and other supported reader-based roles can view consumption dashboards and reports.

claims.quote: The range must select exactly one completed UTC day. Current-day, future, and multi-day ranges are rejected, not clamped.
